PullRequest.Title: Surface extensions blocked by the marketplace
PullRequest.Body:
The Private Marketplace evaluates an administrative allow/deny policy on every extension query, and until now a denial reached the client only as an absence: the extension was simply not in the results, or the install failed, and the developer had nothing to read. That becomes an internal support ticket, fielded by the same administrators who made the decision.

The registry now returns the record carrying a `blocked` flag instead of omitting it. This reads that flag and explains the block.

Implements the client half of the Extension Blocking wire contract (spec in review at `VSMarketplace.Specs` PR 951559). No behaviour changes unless a gallery sets the flag, which no deployed marketplace does yet.

## What it does

Blocked extensions are still returned by the gallery, so enforcement lives at the decision points rather than by filtering them out of results:

- `canInstall`, on both the platform and workbench services
- auto-update, and the auto-update toggle
- the `extensionDisallowInstall` context key
- `ExtensionStatusAction`, where the block takes precedence over deprecation
- the chat `searchExtensionsTool`, alongside the existing deprecated and malicious filters

The message distinguishes an organization policy decision from a marketplace statement. Conflating those either alarms users about a routine policy decision or understates a marketplace finding.

## Two granularities

The flag applies either to a whole extension or to a single version while the others remain available. Both are read, but they are not distinguished in the result.

A blocked version is skipped when selecting a version to acquire, in display paths as well as install paths. A version pinned out by policy is usually the newest one, so selecting it would strand an extension whose earlier versions are perfectly usable. Because of that, a block only reaches a user once no version is permitted at all - and at that point the extension is unavailable to them whichever granularity caused it, so a version-specific message would only send them looking for an alternative that does not exist.

## Install failures now report the actual cause

`canInstall` computes a precise reason, but `checkAndGetCompatibleVersion` discarded it and threw a fixed platform-incompatibility message. That was already wrong for an allow list denial, and adding blocked to the same path would have made a blocked extension claim it was unavailable for the machine's platform.

It now throws the message `canInstall` returned. The error code is deliberately unchanged: both consumers of `IncompatibleTargetPlatform` - settings sync's skip-and-do-not-retry, and the install error dialog - already do the right thing for a blocked extension.

This only affects paths that bypass the disabled install button: settings sync, `--install-extension`, the `vscode:extension/id` URI handler, and workspace recommendations. Those are the ones with no other signal.

## Scope

Only the flag and the origin are read. The contract also defines a `reason`, none of whose values the registry populates today - allow list denials are the only blocks issued, and they carry `origin: policy`. Origin is kept rather than collapsed to a boolean so that a future marketplace-originated block is not attributed to the user's own organization.

Absent, unrecognized, and wrong-typed values degrade to the more severe reading rather than failing the parse, which would have taken down the whole query rather than the one extension.

Not included, and worth a separate discussion: an extension already installed when a block arrives is gated from updating but is not disabled or reported. The sibling states handle that through `EnablementState.DisabledByAllowlist` and the extensions notification, which would need the blocked state persisted onto `ILocalExtension`.

## Testing

Unit tests cover the contract's consumer conformance rules: flag without object, object without flag, whole-token flag matching against unknown tokens, degradation of unrecognized, missing, null, and wrong-typed origins, extension blocks outranking version blocks, and the message wording per origin.

Not yet exercised end to end - no deployed marketplace emits the contract, so that needs a stubbed gallery response.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path, request flags, awaited ordering, and HTTP boundaries are explicit in the code. The POSTs are grouped rather than per extension, and no repository cache is present; only the real-world frequency and network RTT are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Marketplace HTTP requests and response bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For B installed extensions whose latest version is blocked, the resource GETs remain B-way concurrent as before, but all B failures are grouped into one latest-only query POST followed serially by one IncludeVersions POST; the extra POST pair repeats on each uncached update check.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Two additional network round trips delay update resolution and consume extra network I/O; one of those round trips is redundant because the resource response already established that the latest version is unusable.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A compatible latest-version resource response was accepted directly, so the update check completed after the existing per-extension resource GETs without entering the query API fallback.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added blocked bit makes getValidRawGalleryExtensionVersion reject a version-blocked latest resource result. getLatestGalleryExtension then returns NOT_COMPATIBLE, getExtensionsUsingResourceApi retries the affected IDs through a latest-only query, and queryGalleryExtensions rejects the same versions again before issuing its all-versions query.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The RIGHT-side addition `blocked: isBlocked(rawGalleryExtensionVersion.flags, rawGalleryExtensionVersion.blocking)` at line 1394 newly rejects the already-fetched latest resource result and then rejects the repeated latest-only query result, activating both fallback POSTs; pre-diff the same version passed this validation.
Findings.Title: Skip the redundant latest-only fallback for blocked versions
Findings.Impact: Periodic and manual extension update checks that encounter a version-blocked latest release wait for two serial Marketplace POSTs after the existing resource fetches. On high-latency links this can add multiple round-trip times before VS Code can determine the usable older version and schedule updates.
Findings.Evidence: checkForUpdates calls getExtensions with compatible=true for installed extensions. The resource path runs getLatestGalleryExtension for each ID; line 1394 feeds isBlocked into isValidVersion, causing a blocked latest version to produce NOT_COMPATIBLE. getExtensionsUsingResourceApi batches those IDs into getExtensionsUsingQueryApi with the original options, whose default is IncludeLatestVersionOnly. That query reaches the same added check, populates needAllVersions, and only then performs a second query with IncludeVersions. queryRawGalleryExtensions shows each query is an awaited HTTP POST with no cache or coalescing layer.
Findings.Recommendation: Propagate a distinct latest-version-is-blocked fallback result and batch those IDs directly into an IncludeVersions query, skipping the intervening latest-only query while preserving selection of an older permitted version.

Scenarios.Scenario: Marketplace browsing and chat extension search
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initial Marketplace query POST and JSON conversion must complete before the first page is shown or returned to the chat tool. If a latest version is version-blocked, selection waits for one additional grouped IncludeVersions POST before results can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST the gallery page query and parse its JSON response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One POST per requested page, carrying up to the configured page size (50 by default, 10 for chat).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial page query was required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST an IncludeVersions query for page entries whose latest version cannot be selected
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one grouped POST per page for all affected extension IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The blocked flag was ignored, so the latest version was accepted and no all-versions fallback ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one network round trip before the page is returned when a latest version is version-blocked.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A UI page defaults to 50 results and chat requests 10; blocked IDs on a page are deduplicated by extension ID and served by one grouped fallback query, not one POST per result.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The initial query and all-versions fallback are serial. A page has at most one additional grouped fallback query; no limiter or separate coalescing/cache is present.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No in-memory result cache is used in queryRawGalleryExtensions; each page/search issues its POST. Warm HTTP transport may reuse connections, but does not remove the request or response parsing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed blocked predicate, needAllVersions map, awaited POST, and page cardinalities are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of searches containing a version-blocked latest release and actual Marketplace RTT are not measured; the single grouped request bounds the regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: The additional all-versions request is necessary to preserve the requested older-version selection and is already batched, so this browsing path alone is not a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Periodic and manual installed-extension update checks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing latest-version resource GETs must finish before compatibility results are synchronized. For a version-blocked latest release, the changed validation then waits serially for a latest-only query POST and an IncludeVersions query POST before VS Code can determine an older permitted version and schedule auto-update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the latest raw gallery record through the resource API
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent GET per eligible installed extension; this pre-existing cardinality is N.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Compatible latest records completed the lookup directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All concurrent GETs settle before query fallback and update synchronization proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST a grouped latest-only query after blocked latest resource records return NOT_COMPATIBLE
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One POST grouping all B affected IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Blocked metadata was ignored, so compatible resource records did not enter this fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a serial RTT after resource GETs and before the required version-history lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST a grouped IncludeVersions query after the same blocked latest versions fail again
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One POST grouping the same B IDs; response bytes scale with their version histories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No fallback POSTs were made for the blocked flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a second serial RTT before update decisions complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed gallery extensions drive N latest-resource GETs; B version-blocked latest results are grouped into each of two fallback POSTs. The POST count is two per update-check batch, not two per blocked extension, while payload size grows with B and with returned version histories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The N resource GETs run concurrently via Promise.all. After they settle, the two fallback POSTs run serially; update checks are sequenced by the existing delayer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The gallery service has no result cache or negative cache for these calls, so periodic checks repeat the sequence. IDs are grouped within each fallback query but there is no coalescing between the redundant latest query and all-versions query.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the resource NOT_COMPATIBLE result, unchanged options, default IncludeLatestVersionOnly, needAllVersions retry, and uncached HTTP POSTs form a direct call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Policy deployment prevalence, B, version-history sizes, and network RTT are unknown; background scheduling lowers severity, but the two serial requests are certain when triggered.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium network-latency regression because the first fallback POST repeats a latest-only lookup whose blocked outcome is already known; affected IDs can go directly to one batched IncludeVersions request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Installing or updating an extension after gallery selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The common management service reads the existing extensions control manifest, then the new canInstall check rejects a whole-extension block before target-platform compatibility lookup, manifest download, VSIX download, signature work, and filesystem installation. For a permitted older version selected after a version block, the normal compatibility, manifest, and package boundaries remain on the install critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query compatible/gallery versions when the initially selected version cannot be used
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one all-versions gallery query per compatibility fallback for the requested extension; dependency IDs are queried in existing batches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version blocking was ignored and the initially selected compatible version proceeded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before selecting an installable older version.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the selected extension manifest and VSIX/signature assets
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One manifest and package asset set per selected extension/dependency, unchanged after selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same assets were fetched for installations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks installation, but a whole-extension block now returns before these downstream transfers on the common path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write and install downloaded extension package data
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Installation wrote the same package data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing installation work; skipped for whole-extension blocks by the new early canInstall result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One requested extension plus its dependency/extension-pack graph; dependency gallery lookups remain batched by discovered IDs, and blocked entries stop before recursive manifest collection in the common service.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dependency discovery batches gallery IDs but processes returned dependency manifests sequentially in the existing collector; package install concurrency is unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Blocking information rides on the gallery object. No new cache is introduced; the existing control-manifest/gallery behavior remains authoritative.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the common service ordering and gallery fallback; specialized remote enforcement differences are correctness concerns and were not reported as performance findings.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dependency graph size and the frequency of version-specific policy blocks vary, but whole-extension blocks clearly avoid rather than add downstream install work on the common path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: whole-extension checks short-circuit expensive work, and the older-version lookup is necessary when a permitted version may exist.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extensions view status, context menus, gallery synchronization, and auto-update gating
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changed getters and predicates run synchronously during extension refresh/status recomputation. A blocked status returns before the existing gallery-manifest signature check; auto-update gating returns before consent and install scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the extension gallery manifest for unsigned-extension status
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing service lookup during relevant status recomputations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unsigned gallery extensions could reach the manifest lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new blocked branch returns before this lookup, so blocked extensions avoid rather than add it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update local extension metadata when an installed extension lacks a gallery UUID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per matching UUID-less installed extension, independent of blocking changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same metadata update condition and cost existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the changed blocking-origin comparison exactly as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales linearly with the displayed/installed extension count, but the added operations are optional-property comparisons and short string-token parsing during gallery conversion. Change events fire only when blocking origin changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI status recomputation remains serialized by the existing throttler; update scheduling remains delayed/coalesced by existing delayers. The diff adds no new concurrent boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing cached local extension list is invalidated on real change events. Same-origin blocked refreshes are compared and do not fire another event; absent blocking state compares undefined to undefined.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the early returns, origin comparison, and throttler/delayer ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact status recomputation frequency and extension counts vary, but added CPU/allocation per object is small and bounded relative to existing conversion/render work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added in-memory checks are bounded, same-state refreshes are suppressed, and blocked states skip existing network/update work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 10 changed files and traced gallery parsing/version selection, Marketplace search, installed-extension update checks, install compatibility, auto-update gating, status rendering, and chat filtering. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity network regression: version-blocked latest resource results take a redundant latest-only query before the required all-versions query. Other added checks are bounded in-memory work or avoid downstream work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
